rationale: Long-COVID study assigns nerve stimulation and active or placebo smell training. The psychophysical and hedonic outcomes are for those exposures.
Cinnamon wound dressing assesses malodor and discomfort during topical care.
Post-COVID rehabilitation uses inhaled spice odors and clinical smell measures.
Smell training in diabetes-related cognitive impairment measures olfactory function after odor exposure.
Oral cinnamon supplementation is evaluated against ovarian stimulation and oocyte or embryo outcomes.
Post-COVID olfactory training measures odor identification and clinical impairment after training.
The topical cinnamon dressing study assesses wound odor and associated discomfort.
The infant nutrition trial measures acceptability and consumption of flavored lipid supplements.
Radiotherapy study measures dysgeusia and uses an olfactory screen in head and neck cancer.
A cancer study assesses food liking, sensory change and diet preference by questionnaire.
Oral cinnamon essential oil is one of seven oils in a randomized respiratory formulation. Adverse follow-up queries smell changes. The completed record has no posted results.
The older-adult comparison assigns an odor-training device or puzzles and measures smell after training.
Cognitive training in patients receiving breast-cancer chemotherapy includes an odor-recognition assessment.
